subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: For external messaging sources, should OpenClaw move toward message-tool/final-only delivery by default, keep automatic delivery as the compatibility default with opt-in safety knobs, or split the policy by direct chat versus shared room?
rationale: The code can be repaired in several ways, but the safest default changes user-visible channel semantics and the security boundary for private assistant text, so automation should not choose that policy alone.

options.title: Adopt safer external-channel default
options.body: Make external channel delivery final-only or message-tool-only by default with migration/docs/doctor guidance and regression proof for direct, group, streaming, final assembly, and cron paths.

options.title: Keep compatibility default and add opt-ins
options.body: Leave automatic visible replies as the default, land opt-in mitigations such as enforceFinalTag or verbose-off gating, and document that customer-facing channels must opt in.

options.title: Defer to narrower channel fixes
options.body: Keep this issue open but handle Slack, Telegram, WebChat, cron, and Signal as separate channel-specific bugs, accepting longer exposure of the shared root boundary.

recommendation.title: Adopt safer external-channel default
recommendation.body: Make external channel delivery final-only or message-tool-only by default with migration/docs/doctor guidance and regression proof for direct, group, streaming, final assembly, and cron paths.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history and current policy touches place steipete closest to the source-reply/default-delivery decision surface.
